newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sing dollar fall overshadows Singapore stocks.
newsitem.headline: Sing dollar fall overshadows Singapore stocks.

text.p: The fall of the Singapore dollar to a new 30-month low against the U.S. dollar dominated Singapore's stock market on Friday morning, dealers said.
"The main story today is what is happening to the Singapore dollar," said a dealer with a local house.
Dealers said while the magnitude of the fall to beyond 1.46 to the U.S. dollar from 1.43 earlier in July was not yet a major concern, investors were concerned about further weakness.
At 0430 GMT, the Sing dollar was trading at 1.4610/20 to the dollar.
For the moment, retail and institutional interest in U.S.-denominated stocks remained evident.

The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 6.42 points at 1,926.96, underpinned by a 20 cent rise in car distributor Cycle & Carriage to S$12.70 and a 14 cent rise in property firm Wing Tai to S$4.18.
Small-capitalised and selected electronic shares continued to shine, led by drug firm Tianjin Zhingxin and CM Telecom.
Both hit new highs, at US$1.56 and US$0.40 respectively, in active trade, chalking up a total volume of about 20 million shares.
Total market volume was a robust 136.7 million shares with 113 gainers to 216 losers.
